entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Battle of Thermopylae was a pivotal event in the Persian invasion of Greece, fought in 479 BCE. It was a testament to the bravery and sacrifice of the 300 Spartans, led by King Leonidas, who defended the narrow pass of Thermopylae against the invading forces of the Persian Empire.

The battle was a crucial moment in the Greco-Persian Wars, a conflict that would shape the course of Western civilization. The Persians, under the rule of King Xerxes I, sought to conquer Greece and extend their empire into Europe. The Greeks, however, were determined to defend their homeland and their way of life.

The battle itself was a masterclass in tactics, with the Spartans using the terrain to their advantage and inflicting heavy casualties on the Persian forces. Despite being vastly outnumbered, the Spartans held off the Persians for several days, buying time for the Greek army to regroup and launch a counterattack.

The Battle of Thermopylae left a lasting impact on Western history, inspiring generations of warriors and leaders with its story of courage and sacrifice. It also had a profound effect on the development of democracy in Greece, as the battle marked a turning point in the struggle for freedom and self-governance.
